context: A uni student debates a teacher about media bias
purpose: Teach: 講談社/毎日新聞/読売新聞/一流/黒人/反日/シンポジウム/セクション

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、昨日の公開シンポジウムで一つ気になったことがあるんですが。
lines.en: Professor, something bothered me at yesterday's public symposium.
lines.style: Polite university student tone with cautious academic framing.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ああ、あのメディア論のシンポジウムね。何が気になったの?
lines.en: Ah, that media theory symposium. What caught your attention?
lines.style: Warm teacher voice, inviting and slightly amused.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 毎日新聞と読売新聞で、同じ事件の扱いが全然違ったんですよ。
lines.en: Mainichi Shimbun and Yomiuri Shimbun covered the same incident totally differently.
lines.style: Eager argumentative student tone, slightly heated and impatient.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 具体的にはどのセクションで違いを感じたの?
lines.en: Which section specifically felt different to you?
lines.style: Calm professorial probing with gentle follow-up questioning.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 国際面ですね。黒人差別の事件なのに、片方はほとんど触れてなくて、ネットでは「反日だ」って叩かれてるんです。
lines.en: The international page. It was a racial discrimination case, but one barely touched it, and online people attack it as anti-Japanese.
lines.style: Frustrated young intellectual voice voicing generational concerns.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そうね。実は講談社の知り合いから聞いた話だけど、雑誌の現場でも同じプレッシャーに悩んでるそうよ。
lines.en: Right. Actually, an acquaintance at Kodansha told me magazine editors face the same pressure.
lines.style: Thoughtful insider tone sharing privileged professional knowledge.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: じゃあ僕たち学生は、複数の新聞を読み比べるしかないってことですか?
lines.en: So as students, we just have to compare multiple newspapers ourselves?
lines.style: Resigned but earnest student seeking practical guidance from mentor.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そう。「これが正解」って決めつけない姿勢が、一流の読み手を作るのよ。
lines.en: Exactly. Refusing to declare one answer correct is what makes a first-rate reader.
lines.style: Concluding teacher tone, firm and gently encouraging throughout.
